$comment: FROZEN V1 NEW-param order. Immutable snapshot of the ordinal↔name assignment used by the shipped OB-Xf editor. NEVER regenerate, NEVER edit — see provenance. Exists solely so a later task can migrate saved localStorage state (positional 108-length arrays) to name-keyed state.

provenance.what: Ordered list of the 28 OB-Xf SynthParams that have NO legacy OB-Xd ancestor. In the shipped UI these are assigned sentinel indices NEW_PARAM_BASE(200)+N by src/obxd-synth-ui.ts, where N is the 0-based ordinal in which controls with no legacy mapping are encountered while walking the obxfControls array in src/obxf-layout.ts (the only live build path: buildObxdSynthUi(grid) in src/obxd-rack.ts:214, synth mode, no target).
provenance.why_frozen: The ordinal scheme is baked into saved user state in localStorage: app-state.ts bulk dumps 108 params per synth instance (and per drum layer); positions 80..107 hold these 28 values at position 80+N (src/obxd-processor.tail.js 'dump_all_params'/'dump_drum_params' write params[base+80+n] = _obxd_get_param(i, 200+n)). The sentinel assignment is about to be replaced with name-keyed lookup; this file is the migration key from old positions to names.

derived_from.lines: 99-161 (idToLegacyIndex build, ID_ALIASES, NEW_PARAM_BASE=200, resolveLegacyIndex), 924-930 (paramBound filter + NEW_PARAM_IDS.push(c.id) in encounter order), 827 (NEW_PARAM_IDS reset per build)
derived_from.role: the ordinal sentinel assignment being frozen

derived_from.lines: 93-573 (obxfControls array — array order IS the encounter order)
16-179 (paramMappings — streaming ids that DO have a legacy index and therefore never fall through to sentinels)

331-363 (apply_new_param_instance switch: offset→engine method), 800-829 (new_param_names[] table: streaming name→offset), 634-640 (apply_param_instance sentinel dispatch), 1853-1885 (obxd_set/get_drum_layer_param, idx-200 = g_drum_layer_new offset)

derived_from.role: proof that saved-state position = 80 + sentinel offset

verification.method: Manual walk of obxfControls (paramBound !== false, alias-resolved streaming id absent from paramMappings.newId ⇒ sentinel) cross-checked against a mechanical derivation that imports the real src/obxf-layout.ts + src/obxf-param-mappings.ts modules and replicates resolveLegacyIndex verbatim. Both agree 28/28. Every offset then compared against the C-side new_param_names[] table.
verification.result: 28/28 offsets semantically match the C-side table (same param at every offset). Exactly one NAME-STRING divergence: offset 5 — TS control id 'RingModVol' (layout) vs canonical streaming name 'RingModMix' (C table, tests, .fxp schema). Same underlying param, same offset, same engine method processRingModVolume — an alias duality, NOT an offset desync. See tools/NEW_PARAM_ORDER_NOTES.md.

anomalies.detail: Offset 5's layout control id is 'RingModVol' (src/obxf-layout.ts, Mixer section, widgetName 'ringModVolKnob'); the canonical SynthParam::ID streaming name is 'RingModMix' (used by the C-side new_param_names[] table, test/obxf-dispatch-coverage.test.ts, and the .fxp named-attribute schema). NEW_PARAM_IDS in obxd-synth-ui.ts therefore logs 'RingModVol' at position 5 while every other consumer uses 'RingModMix'. Same offset, same engine method (processRingModVolume) — no runtime desync in the synth path. The name-keyed replacement MUST accept both spellings (see nameAliases) or keyed lookups on either side will miss.

If buildObxdSynthUi is ever called WITH a target (drumMode=true), the DRUM_INACTIVE_* filters remove 12 of the 28 NEW-param controls BEFORE the build loop, so the surviving 16 would be assigned sentinels 200..215 in a SHIFTED order (e.g. Filter4PoleXpander would land at 200, which the engine interprets as UnisonVoices). This path is currently DEAD CODE (the only live call is obxd-rack.ts:214 with no target; the drum UI uses drum-rack.ts knob strips whose hard-coded sentinels — lines 118-135 — match THIS frozen order). Recorded so the name-keyed replacement does not resurrect the shifted path.
